data.body:
Change 2988 has been sitting at `Verified -1` since 2026-09-19 03:33 UTC. Root-caused
and fixed; the change is amended, rebased onto current `origin/main`, and
`make verify` is running before the re-push.

## The failure

CI failed identically on all three matrix cells -- py3.11, py3.12, py3.13 -- with
2 failures against 20,414 passes (run 35418894254). Both come from the one new
file the change adds, `tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py`, and both are whole-tree
AST policy scans rather than anything about the entrypoint behaviour under test.
Neither is visible to `make lint`, which is the trap AGENTS.md documents.

**1. `test_bare_clone_source_upkeep_sweep.py` -- 10 findings.**

    tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py:56:  clones unpinned bare repository 'remote' via a clone argv
    tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py:105: clones unpinned bare repository 'remote' via _clone()
    ... 8 more _clone() sites

**2. `test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py` -- 2 offenders**, at lines 14 and 85.

## Root cause

The 10 sweep findings are ONE defect, not ten. Reading the sweep's own detection
rule: a name is bare-by-hand when a `--bare` git argv binds it, and
`init_bare_remote` / `apply_upkeep_pins` deliberately do not bind such a name, "which
is the point". Only line 56's `git clone --bare` bound `remote`; the 9 `_clone()`
findings were downstream consequences of that single unpinned binding. Fixing the
one creation site clears all 10.

The hazard the sweep exists for is real and measured, not stylistic. At git's
defaults a push into a bare repository leaves a detached `git maintenance run` child
repacking and pruning `objects/` after the push has returned, and a LOCAL clone walks
that directory wholesale, so it races the pruner and dies with exit 128. Measured on
git 2.55: unpinned 5/960 clones exited 128, pinned 0/960. Landing this file as
written would have introduced a new flake source into the suite.

The 2 env offenders are a separate convention with its own reason: pytest prints
function arguments in its default long traceback, so a plain `dict(os.environ)` passed
to a subprocess dumps every inherited environment value -- including secrets -- into
CI output on any subprocess startup failure. `_subprocess_env.subprocess_env()`
returns a `dict` subclass whose `__repr__` redacts.

## Fix

Three edits, all in the new test file, no change to `mcp-entrypoint.sh` or the runbook:

- `_init_remote` now builds the remote with
  `init_bare_remote(tmp_path / "remote.git", initial_branch="main")` and pushes into
  it, replacing the `git clone --bare`. The helper applies the pins in the same call
  that creates the repository, so there is no window in which a push reaches an
  unpinned remote.
- `_git`'s env is now `subprocess_env(GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=..., ...)`.
- `_run_provision`'s env is now `subprocess_env(MCP_CODE_DIR=..., ...)`.
- `import os` dropped, now unused.

## Verification

Both previously-failing scans pass: 25 passed. The file's own 8 tests still pass, so
the `_init_remote` restructure is behaviour-preserving -- the remote is seeded by
push instead of by clone, and every assertion holds unchanged.

Rebased onto `e84e4c5e9439bcfd27875d152de36eb40eb4f46b`. `Change-Id`
`I24deb7541321ef85edd5c9e93d15970805480033` preserved, so this uploads as a new
patch set rather than a duplicate change.
